messages:
elaine: ran into a weird SSE parsing edge during a partner demo. node-sdk v1.4.2 + sampleapp v0.11. If the client aborts and reconnects within ~200ms some `data:` lines from the previous connection get concatenated with the first `data:` of the new connection and the parser emits a single JSON blob.

elaine: Minimal repro (loopback): start stream -> send one event w/o trailing blank line -> kill client -> reconnect fast -> send next event. Sometimes parsed as one event `{...}\n{...}` instead of two separate events.

jong: is it a FIN vs RST thing? kernel might still have bytes in TCP buffers.

elaine: tcpdump shows FIN in most runs but timing varies. the real issue seems to be parser buffer not being cleared on socket close/end.

rafa: seen this before. node parser holds a partial buffer until it sees a blank-line delimiter. on abrupt close the buffer remains and then new bytes append. cheap fix: on socket `close`/`end` force-flush or drop partial buffer. safer: emit a comment marker so downstream JSON parsers don't crash.

jong: can we treat a leading `event:`/`id:` as implicit delimiter? that'll avoid merging when next connection starts with an `id:` line.

elaine: tried both approaches. forced flush on close + comment prefix `:partial` worked for demo. pushed a small patch to local branch that emits `:partial` then the truncated payload and resets buffer. prevents JSON parse errors for consumers by making it a comment.

rafa: please add unit test that reproduces exact kernel race: spawn child that connects and exits without sending trailing CRLF, then new connection sends next event. CI should run that on loopback.

jong: also add an opt-in SDK flag `sseAggressiveFlush` default false to avoid behavioral change for users who rely on strict event boundaries. docs should mention tradeoff.

elaine: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/820 — includes parser change + test harness. CI flaky on one case, investigating.

ci-bot: Created issue DEVEX-2167: "sse parser: partial buffer survives fast reconnect -> merged data events" (link: https://tracker.internal/DEVEX-2167)

rafa: long-term we should add small sequence numbers in `id:` when possible so clients can detect out-of-order/merged frames. servers can optionally include `id` header. also server-side flush (`\n\n` and socket flush) helps but doesn't fully solve kernel races.

elaine: agreed. will land patch behind flag and backport to 1.3.x afterwards. i'll also add a short note in docs/streaming.md about immediate reconnect edge-case and recommend sample backends always send final blank line and flush.

jong: thanks. good catch catching it before demo.
